sources.entry: Lightdash | BI tool for dbt projects

summary.one_liner: Lightdash is an open-source agentic BI platform that builds governed metrics, dashboards, AI agents, and data apps on top of a context layer (dbt projects or standalone YAML) pointed at a data warehouse.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a context layer where metrics, dimensions, joins, descriptions, caching, and access rules are defined once and reused across dashboards, AI agents, data apps, embedded analytics, SDKs, and an MCP server. Charts, dashboards, and metrics can be kept as files ("BI as code") that are previewed from a CLI, validated in CI, and reviewed in pull requests. Lightdash agents answer questions from that context layer and return inspectable queries, and business users can ask questions in plain English. Embedding is supported through an SDK with configurable row-level security and user attributes. The core BI platform can be self-hosted, and the README lists warehouse adapters for BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Databricks, Postgres, Trino, ClickHouse, and more.
use_cases: define governed company metrics in one place
ask business questions in plain English with AI
review analytics changes in pull requests
embed dashboards in a customer-facing product
self-host a BI tool on own infrastructure
notable: BI as code: charts, dashboards, and metrics are stored as files and reviewed through PRs and CI
Context layer shared by dashboards, AI agents, data apps, embedding, and MCP
AI agents return inspectable queries and respect permissions
Lightdash CLI with preview and validate commands for coding-agent workflows
Open-source core with optional commercial enterprise features
caveats: Cloud is the recommended path; self-hosting requires managing your own infrastructure
Enterprise features on self-hosted deployments require a license key from the Lightdash team
Some features (AI agents, data apps, managed upgrades) are presented as Cloud-first
keywords: ask questions about data in plain english
